belief: God only hears the prayers of good people.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that God only hears the prayers of good people, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Feeling too sinful or unworthy to pray. Verses about God hearing “the righteous” read as “perfect people only.” Comparing yourself with people who seem holier. Shame about recent sins. A belief that you must clean up before you can talk to God.
teaches: Scripture says God hears the righteous, but it also shows that the righteous are not perfect people; they are humble people who turn to Him. God does not despise a broken and contrite heart. The tax collector beat his breast and asked for mercy, and Jesus said he went home justified. The LORD is near to all who call on Him in truth. Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. God does not wait for you to be good; He invites you to come as you are.
self_statements: God won’t listen to someone like me.
I have to be good before I can pray.
I’m too far gone for God to hear me.
I’ll pray when I get my life together.
errors: Calling yourself too bad for God to hear.
Comparing yourself to people who seem holier.
Staying away from God until you feel worthy.
questions: What kind of heart does God not despise?
What did the tax collector pray, and what happened?
Who is the LORD near to, according to Psalm 145:18?
What does Romans 10:13 say about everyone who calls?
Am I waiting to be good before I come to God?
Is my sin a reason to avoid God or a reason to run to Him?
What would I say to God right now if I believed He would listen?
truth: God does not only hear the prayers of good people. He hears the humble and broken-hearted who call on Him. The LORD is near to all who call on Him in truth. I don’t have to clean up first; I can come as I am, ask for mercy, and know that He hears me.
hw_questions: What kind of heart does God not despise?
What happened to the tax collector?
Who is the LORD near to?
Am I waiting to be good first?
Is my sin a reason to avoid God or run to Him?
hw_truths: God does not despise a broken and contrite heart.
The LORD is near to all who call on Him.
I can come to God as I am.
God hears the humble who ask for mercy.
Everyone who calls on the Lord will be saved.
My sin is a reason to run to God, not away.
log: Each day, pray one honest prayer for mercy and write: “He hears me.”
name_example: Sarah called out, and the LORD heard her; He saved her from all her troubles.
actions: Pray the tax collector’s prayer each morning:
“God, have mercy on me, a sinner,” and then thank Him for hearing.

prayer: Father, thank You that You do not despise a broken and contrite heart. Help me reject the lie that You only hear the prayers of good people. I come to You as I am. God, have mercy on me, a sinner. Thank You that You hear me. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
